name: copy_to
declaration: const unsafe fn copy_to (self , dest : NonNull < T > , count : usize) where T : Sized ,
documentation:
Copies `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes from `self` to `dest`. The source
 and destination may overlap.

 NOTE: this has the *same* argument order as [`ptr::copy`].

 See [`ptr::copy`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::copy`]: crate::ptr::copy()
rules: self must be valid for reads of count * size_of::<T>() bytes.
dest must be valid for writes of count * size_of::<T>() bytes and must remain valid while self is read for count * size_of::<T>() bytes, including when the source and destination ranges overlap.
self must be properly aligned for T, even when count * size_of::<T>() is 0.
dest must be properly aligned for T, even when count * size_of::<T>() is 0.
The source and destination memory ranges may overlap.
The copied data may be uninitialized or otherwise violate the requirements of T.
The initialization state of the copied data is preserved exactly.
If T is not Copy, using both the values in the region beginning at self and the region beginning at dest after the bitwise copy can violate memory safety.
